common_steps: Check several plants across the field before deciding how widespread it is.
Ask your local agriculture officer, Krishi Vigyan Kendra or the Kisan Call Centre (1800-180-1551) before any spraying.

apple.label: Apple___Apple_scab
apple.name: Apple scab
steps: Collect and destroy fallen infected leaves.
Prune to let air and sunlight into the tree.

apple.label: Apple___Black_rot
apple.name: Apple black rot
steps: Cut out dead branches and cankers.
Remove dried, shrivelled fruit from the tree and ground.

apple.label: Apple___Cedar_apple_rust
apple.name: Apple rust
steps: Remove nearby juniper or cedar hosts where practical.
Collect and destroy badly affected leaves.

cherry.label: Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew
cherry.name: Powdery mildew (cherry)
steps: Prune crowded shoots to improve air flow.
Remove heavily coated leaves.

grape.label: Grape___Black_rot
grape.name: Black rot (grape)
steps: Remove mummified berries and infected leaves.
Keep the canopy open for air flow.

grape.label: Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles)
grape.name: Esca / black measles (grape)
steps: Mark affected vines and prune out dead wood in dry weather.
Clean pruning tools between vines.

grape.label: Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spot)
grape.name: Leaf spot (grape)
steps: Remove spotted leaves and fallen debris.
Avoid wetting leaves when irrigating.

maize.label: Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_spot
maize.name: Grey leaf spot (maize)
steps: Plough in or remove old maize residue after harvest.
Rotate with a non-cereal crop next season.

maize.label: Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_
maize.name: Common rust (maize)
steps: Note how many plants show rust pustules.
Choose a rust-tolerant variety next season.

maize.label: Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight
maize.name: Leaf blight (maize)
steps: Remove or plough in infected residue after harvest.
Rotate crops and use a tolerant variety next season.

orange.label: Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening)
orange.name: Citrus greening
steps: There is no cure for infected trees; get it confirmed by an expert.
Watch for small psyllid insects on new shoots and report them.

peach.label: Peach___Bacterial_spot
peach.name: Bacterial spot (peach)
steps: Prune to improve air flow.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

pepper.label: Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot
pepper.name: Bacterial spot (capsicum)
steps: Remove badly spotted leaves.
Avoid working among plants when they are wet.
Use healthy, certified seed or seedlings next season.

potato.label: Potato___Early_blight
potato.name: Early blight (potato)
steps: Remove lower leaves with target-like brown spots.
Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress.

potato.label: Potato___Late_blight
potato.name: Late blight (potato)
potato.cause: fungus-like organism; spreads fast in cool, wet weather
steps: Act quickly: it can spread across a field in days in cool, humid weather.
Remove and destroy infected plants; do not leave them in the field.
Contact your agriculture officer or the Kisan Call Centre today.

squash.label: Squash___Powdery_mildew
squash.name: Powdery mildew (gourds)
steps: Remove heavily coated leaves.
Give plants more space for air flow.

strawberry.label: Strawberry___Leaf_scorch
strawberry.name: Leaf scorch (strawberry)
steps: Remove infected leaves.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

tomato.label: Tomato___Bacterial_spot
tomato.name: Bacterial spot (tomato)
steps: Remove badly spotted leaves.
Avoid splashing water on leaves.
Use healthy seedlings next season.

tomato.label: Tomato___Early_blight
tomato.name: Early blight (tomato)
steps: Remove lower leaves with brown ring-like spots.
Mulch the soil so splashes do not reach the leaves.
Rotate away from tomato, potato and chilli next season.

tomato.label: Tomato___Late_blight
tomato.name: Late blight (tomato)
tomato.cause: fungus-like organism; spreads fast in cool, wet weather
steps: Act quickly: it can spread across a field in days in cool, humid weather.
Remove and destroy infected plants.
Contact your agriculture officer or the Kisan Call Centre today.

tomato.label: Tomato___Leaf_Mold
tomato.name: Leaf mould (tomato)
steps: Improve air flow by pruning and wider spacing.
Reduce humidity in protected cultivation.

tomato.label: Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot
tomato.name: Septoria leaf spot (tomato)
steps: Remove spotted lower leaves.
Avoid wetting leaves when irrigating.

tomato.label: Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider_mite
tomato.name: Spider mites (tomato)
steps: Look under leaves for tiny moving dots and fine webbing.
Remove badly infested leaves; mites increase in hot, dry weather.

tomato.label: Tomato___Target_Spot
tomato.name: Target spot (tomato)
steps: Remove infected lower leaves.
Improve air flow between plants.

tomato.label: Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus
tomato.name: Leaf curl virus (tomato)
steps: There is no cure for infected plants; pull out and destroy badly affected plants early.
Check for whiteflies under leaves; use yellow sticky traps to monitor them.

tomato.label: Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus
tomato.name: Mosaic virus (tomato)
steps: Pull out and destroy infected plants.
Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants; avoid tobacco use near plants.
